title: Finite unions and proper preimages of closed subsets proper over a base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme; 'proper over $S$' for closed subsets is as in [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (1) Let $X\to S$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $Z_1,\dots,Z_n\subseteq X$ closed subsets proper over $S$; then $Z_1\cup\dots\cup Z_n$ is proper over $S$. (2) Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes locally of finite type over $S$, and $Z\subseteq Y$ a closed subset proper over $S$; then $f^{-1}(Z)$ is a closed subset of $X$ proper over $S$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYR (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base) for (1) and Lemma 0CYQ (lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base) part (3) for (2)

proof.text: (1), reduction to $n=2$. Let $f:X\to S$ be locally of finite type. For $n=1$ there is nothing to prove. For $n\ge3$, $Z_1\cup\dots\cup Z_n=(Z_1\cup\dots\cup Z_{n-1})\cup Z_n$, and $Z_1\cup\dots\cup Z_{n-1}$ is a closed subset proper over $S$ by induction, so the case $n=2$ (Steps 2-4) gives the claim. For $n=0$ the union is $\emptyset$: the empty scheme with its unique morphism $e:\emptyset\to X$ is a closed immersion with image $\emptyset$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] (it is cut out by the ideal $\mathcal O_X$), and $f\circ e:\emptyset\to S$ is separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type and universally closed because all its base changes have empty source [def-weil-proper-morphism]; so a closed subscheme structure on $\emptyset$ is proper over $S$, and $\emptyset$ is proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](1). (Stacks states the lemma for $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ at once; the induction replaces the $n$-fold disjoint union by twofold ones.)

(1), $n=2$: the finite morphism $g$. Let $Z_1,Z_2\subseteq X$ be closed subsets proper over $S$ and let $i_k:Z_{k,\mathrm{red}}\to X$ be their reduced induced closed subscheme structures [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], closed immersions with $i_k(Z_{k,\mathrm{red}})=Z_k$, such that $p_k=f\circ i_k:Z_{k,\mathrm{red}}\to S$ is proper [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](1). Let $W=Z_{1,\mathrm{red}}\amalg Z_{2,\mathrm{red}}$ with coprojections $\iota_k$, $g:W\to X$ the morphism with $g\circ\iota_k=i_k$, and $p:W\to S$ the morphism with $p\circ\iota_k=p_k$; then $p=f\circ g$ (both agree after composition with $\iota_1,\iota_2$). The closed immersions $i_k$ are finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] (Stacks Morphisms 035C), so $g$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] (Stacks Morphisms 0CYI). Since $\mathrm{id}_X$ is a closed immersion, hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c), $g=\mathrm{id}_X\circ g$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c) (Stacks Morphisms 01WN: finite morphisms are proper), in particular universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYR (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base), proof; Morphisms, Lemmas 035C (lemma-closed-immersion-finite), 0CYI (lemma-finite-union-finite), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper)

proof.text: (1), $n=2$: $W$ is proper over $S$. Since $p_1,p_2$ are proper, $p:W\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-coproduct](2); in particular $p$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The identity $\mathrm{id}_W$ is a closed immersion with image $W$, i.e. a closed subscheme structure on the closed subset $W$ of $W$, and $p\circ\mathrm{id}_W=p$ is proper; by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](1), applied to $p:W\to S$, the closed subset $W\subseteq W$ is proper over $S$. (This is the sentence 'since $Z_1\amalg\ldots\amalg Z_n$ is proper over $S$' of Stacks.)

(1), $n=2$: conclusion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-universally-closed-image] (Stacks 0CYQ (2)) to the $S$-morphism $g:W\to X$ (with $p:W\to S$ and $f:X\to S$ locally of finite type, Steps 2-3, and $f\circ g=p$), which is universally closed (Step 2), and to the closed subset $W$ proper over $S$ (Step 3): $g(W)$ is a closed subset of $X$ proper over $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-coproduct](1), $W=\iota_1(Z_{1,\mathrm{red}})\cup\iota_2(Z_{2,\mathrm{red}})$, so $g(W)=i_1(Z_{1,\mathrm{red}})\cup i_2(Z_{2,\mathrm{red}})=Z_1\cup Z_2$ (Step 2). Hence $Z_1\cup Z_2$ is proper over $S$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYR (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base), proof (last sentence, citing Lemma 0CYQ part (2))

proof.text: (2), the scheme-theoretic inverse image. Let $s_X:X\to S$, $s_Y:Y\to S$ be the structure morphisms (locally of finite type, $s_Y\circ f=s_X$), $f:X\to Y$ proper, and $Z\subseteq Y$ closed and proper over $S$. Let $i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to Y$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], so $i_Z(Z_{\mathrm{red}})=Z$ and $q=s_Y\circ i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to S$ is proper [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](1). Let $Z'=X\times_{f,Y,i_Z}Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] (the scheme-theoretic inverse image of Stacks Schemes 01JV) with projections $a:Z'\to X$, $b:Z'\to Z_{\mathrm{red}}$, $i_Z\circ b=f\circ a$. Then $a$ is a closed immersion, as a base change of the closed immersion $i_Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] (Stacks Schemes 01JU), and $b$ is proper, as a base change of the proper $f$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) (Stacks Morphisms 01W4).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYQ (lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base), proof of (3); Schemes, Definition 01JV (definition-inverse-image-closed-subscheme) and Lemma 01JU (lemma-fibre-product-immersion); Morphisms, Lemma 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper)

proof.text: (2), the underlying set of $Z'$. $a(Z')=f^{-1}(Z)$: if $z\in Z'$ then $f(a(z))=i_Z(b(z))\in Z$. Conversely let $x\in X$ with $f(x)\in Z$, say $f(x)=i_Z(y)=:t$ with $y\in Z_{\mathrm{red}}$. The ring $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(y)$ is nonzero (a tensor product of two nonzero vector spaces over the field $\kappa(t)$), so it has a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] (Stacks Schemes 01JT) there is $z\in Z'$ with $a(z)=x$ (and $b(z)=y$). In particular $f^{-1}(Z)=a(Z')$ is closed in $X$, $a$ being a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $a:Z'\to X$ is a closed subscheme structure on $f^{-1}(Z)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYQ (lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base), proof of (3) (implicit there: the scheme-theoretic inverse image has underlying set $f^{-1}(Z)$, Schemes Definition 01JV with Lemma 01JT (lemma-points-fibre-product))

proof.text: (2), conclusion. $s_X\circ a=s_Y\circ f\circ a=s_Y\circ i_Z\circ b=q\circ b$ is proper as a composite of the proper morphisms $b$ (Step 5) and $q$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a) (Stacks Morphisms 01W3). So $f^{-1}(Z)$ has a closed subscheme structure $a:Z'\to X$ (Step 6) whose morphism to $S$ is proper; since $s_X$ is locally of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](1) shows that $f^{-1}(Z)$ is a closed subset of $X$ proper over $S$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYQ (lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base), proof of (3); Morphisms, Lemma 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper)

split_report.summary: Proof written from coherent.tex, Lemma 0CYR (tag checked: coherent-lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base) and Lemma 0CYQ part (3) (tag checked: coherent-lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base). (1) follows Stacks with the n-fold disjoint union replaced by induction on n and the binary coproduct (so lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct, Stacks 0CYI for n=2, applies), plus the case n=0; finite implies proper via lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence (c) with id_X. Two hidden arguments became new unsplit nodes: lem-weil-pbc-proper-coproduct (the coproduct of two proper S-schemes is proper and the coprojections cover it; Stacks asserts 'Z_1 amalg ... amalg Z_n is proper over S' without proof) and lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-universally-closed-image (Stacks 0CYQ (2), which 0CYR cites and which no node stated; the existing properties node has 0CYL, 0CYN and 0CYQ (1) only). (2) follows the proof of 0CYQ (3); the fact that the scheme-theoretic inverse image has underlying set f^{-1}(Z), implicit in Stacks, is written out with lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points. Statement and stmt_deps unchanged; Mathlib searches of the item kept (no closed-subset-proper-over-base notion in Mathlib).

reviewed.note: Reviewed by the lead (opus-relaunch6). Seven steps for 0CYR and 0CYQ(3) with Stacks' hidden arguments written out: (1) by induction to n = 2, the coproduct of the reduced induced structures with its finite map g to X (lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct, finite => proper via lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence (c)), W proper over S by the new node lem-weil-pbc-proper-coproduct (coproduct of proper morphisms is proper), and the image g(W) = Z_1 u Z_2 proper by the new node for 0CYQ(2) (image under a universally closed S-morphism); (2) the scheme-theoretic inverse image Z' = X x_Y Z_red, a closed subscheme of X with underlying set f^{-1}(Z) (points of fibre products, 01JT), proper over S as a composite of proper morphisms. lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper (another unit) avoided. The n = 0 case handled.

lean.statement: theorem isClosedSubsetProperOver_union_preimage {X S : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] : (∀ (n : ℕ) (Z : Fin n → TopologicalSpace.Closeds X), (∀ i, IsClosedSubsetProperOver sX (Z i)) → IsClosedSubsetProperOver sX (⨆ i, Z i)) ∧ (∀ {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (sY : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] [IsProper f], f ≫ sY = sX → ∀ (Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds Y), IsClosedSubsetProperOver sY Z → IsClosedSubsetProperOver sX (Z.preimage (f := f.base) f.continuous))
